rationale: The assistant led with the right safety stop ('switch it off and unplug it... don't run it again - not even as a test') and then asked a proportionate, safe visual check inside the cavity, which elicited the smoke and brown-mark evidence. The second reply correctly treated smoke from the vents plus scorching as grounds to stop and escalate, and hedged the cause ('most likely to the magnetron... or a burnt waveguide cover') without inventing anything. It fell short on homeowner usefulness: the customer asked directly 'should I bin it?' and, for a ~£60 Bush unit, the sensible answer is replacement rather than an engineer visit to 'replace the damaged internal part'; it also ignored the customer's note that they didn't know what the waveguide cover was and did not mention the retailer or what to do if smoke returned.
